moments.summary: Reduced before-and-after to a skill around agent-browser and gh.

sources.title: [skill] Reduce before-and-after to agent-browser + gh
sources.text: Turns `before-and-after` into a thin skill around `agent-browser` and `gh --attach`. Browser capture and Vercel access stay with their source tool; this package now owns PR formatting, attachment publishing, and guidance for intelligent captures.
sources.descriptionHtml: Turns before-and-after into a thin skill around agent-browser and gh --attach. Browser capture and Vercel access stay with their source tool; this package now owns PR formatting, attachment publishing, and guidance for intelligent captures.

parts.text: New version of our /before-and-after skill is live, making it easier for agents to add visual proof to PRs. Try it out!
• Files upload directly to GitHub with the new
• Bypasses preview deployment protection using agent-browser's bundled skill

moments.summary: Shipped 30 fps recording by default, with support for 60 fps.

sources.title: [cli] Record at 30 fps by default, up to 60, from Page.startScreencast
sources.text: Video recording captured 10 fps by polling `Page.captureScreenshot` on a fixed interval, so scrolls, hovers, and transitions came out as a slideshow. Recording now defaults to 30 fps, accepts `--fps` from 1 to 60, and takes its frames from `Page.startScreencast` on a dedicated CDP session, so a 60 fps take actually holds 60 distinct pictures per second.
sources.descriptionHtml: Video recording captured 10 fps by polling Page.captureScreenshot on a fixed interval, so scrolls, hovers, and transitions came out as a slideshow. Recording now defaults to 30 fps, accepts --fps from 1 to 60, and takes its frames from Page.startScreencast on a dedicated CDP session, so a 60 fps take actually holds 60 distinct pictures per second.

parts.text: can now capture video at 60 fps, making it easy to add proof of polish :)
